text.p: The 10-year cash narrowed the spread with the Bunds and should continue firm even if the market remains uncertain about the prospects for monetary union.
The nervousness about whether southern European countries will be included in the group to launch the single currency in 1999 will probably cap advances in the Portuguese market, traders said.

"The tone is positive and the spread (with the 10-year Bund) is going to continue slightly below 120 basis points," said one trader. "But there is still a lot of caution about monetary union", he added.
But traders noted that most of the activity on Friday was trading business with little or no end-user interest.
"For the end-users, it is important that there is a new groundswell in favour of our entry into monetary union. The memory of last week's sell-off is still vivid," said one trader.
Traders said that the short end of the curve could benefit if money market rates react to the strength of the dollar and the escudo by easing.
